AeroShield: Active Electromagnetic Nanoscale Shield for Space Dust Repulsion

AeroShield is an active electromagnetic nanoscale shield designed to repel razor-sharp lunar and Martian dust from spacesuits. By integrating carbon nanotubes into fabrics and applying transparent conductive coatings, the system uses Coulomb’s Law to deflect micro-dust before contact. Lightweight and energy-efficient, AeroShield ensures ultimate astronaut safety and mission longevity in deep space.
summary: AeroShield is an active electromagnetic nanoscale shield inspired by NASA’s lunar regolith research and Electrodynamic Dust Shield (EDS) studies. Designed to mitigate abrasive lunar and Martian dust on spacesuits and exploration hardware, it integrates Carbon Nanotubes (CNTs) and Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) coatings. By applying Coulomb’s Law principles, AeroShield generates a dynamic repulsive electrostatic field to prevent regolith adhesion, ensuring enhanced astronaut safety and mission longevity.
details:
What it does & How it works:

Utilizing NASA’s lunar regolith characterization data and research on electrostatic dust mitigation, AeroShield creates a localized repulsive field across spacesuit outer layers. By combining transparent Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) conductive traces with embedded Carbon Nanotubes (CNTs), it applies Coulomb’s Law to actively repel charged regolith particles before they adhere or cause abrasion.

Key Benefits & Impact:

Directly addresses the critical dust hazards documented in NASA’s Apollo missions and Artemis program research—protecting suit seals, visors, and mechanical joints from abrasion, thermal degradation, and respiratory toxicity.

Tools & Technologies Used:

NASA Lunar Regolith & Dust Mitigation Research Data, nanotechnology material modeling, UI/UX prototyping, and AI-assisted research synthesis.
